questions.stem: Which of the following reactions produce(s) propane as a major product?
questions.solution: Heating sodium butanoate with soda-lime removes CO₂, so (A) gives propane. Kolbe electrolysis of butanoate couples two propyl radicals, giving hexane, so (B) does not. Zn/dil. HCl reduces 1-chloropropane to propane, so (C) works. Zinc removes both bromines from 1,2-dibromopropane as ZnBr₂ and forms a C=C, giving propene, so (D) does not.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: Choose the correct option(s) that give(s) an aromatic compound as the major product

options.text: i) alc. KOH ii) NaNH₂ iii) red hot iron tube, 873 K

questions.solution: (A) Double dehydrobromination of 1,2-dibromopropane (alc. KOH, then NaNH₂) gives propyne, which trimerises in a red-hot iron tube to mesitylene, which is aromatic. (B) Methoxide removes the acidic CH₂ proton of cyclopentadiene, giving the cyclopentadienyl anion, a planar ring with 6 π electrons, which is aromatic. (C) Elimination from 3-bromocyclobutene would give cyclobutadiene, which is antiaromatic, so it is not correct. (D) Benzene with excess Cl₂ under UV first adds chlorine to give hexachlorocyclohexane; the answer treats the forcing 500 K conditions as giving an aromatic chlorobenzene product (BHC readily loses HCl to give trichlorobenzene).

check.note: Held back for review: answers differ

questions.stem:
Choose the correct option(s) for the following reaction sequence
4-MeOC₆H₄–C≡C–CH₂–CHO —i) Hg²⁺, dil. H₂SO₄ ii) AgNO₃, NH₄OH iii) Zn-Hg, conc. HCl→ Q —i) SOCl₂, pyridine ii) AlCl₃→ R —Zn-Hg, conc. HCl→ S
Consider Q, R and S as major products
questions.solution: Hg²⁺-catalysed hydration puts the C=O on the alkyne carbon next to the anisyl ring, giving ArCOCH₂CH₂CHO. Tollens reagent oxidises the CHO to CO₂H, and Clemmensen reduction removes the ketone, so Q is 4-(4-methoxyphenyl)butanoic acid. The acid chloride cyclises by intramolecular Friedel–Crafts acylation onto the ring carbon ortho to the chain, giving R = 7-methoxy-1-tetralone. A second Clemmensen reduction gives S = 6-methoxytetralin. Options C (Q, R) and D (R, S) are both correct.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: Choose the correct option(s) from the following

options.text: Natural rubber is polyisoprene containing trans alkene units
Teflon is prepared by heating tetrafluoroethene in presence of a persulphate catalyst at high pressure
Cellulose has only α-D-glucose units that are joined by glycosidic linkages

questions.solution: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene; the trans polymer is gutta-percha, so (A) is false. Nylon-6, made from caprolactam, is a polyamide with –CO–NH– links, so (B) is true. Teflon is made by heating tetrafluoroethene under high pressure with a persulphate initiator, so (C) is true. Cellulose is built from β-D-glucose units joined by β-1,4-glycosidic links, not α-units, so (D) is false.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Total number of hydroxyl groups present in a molecule of the major product P is ____
substrate —i) H₂, Pd-BaSO₄, quinoline ii) dil. KMnO₄ (excess), 273 K→ P
questions.solution: Lindlar hydrogenation reduces only the C≡C, to a cis C=C, and leaves the two ring double bonds alone. The substrate now has three C=C bonds: the new acyclic one and one in each ring. Cold dilute KMnO₄ in excess syn-dihydroxylates every C=C, adding two OH groups to each. P therefore has 3 × 2 = 6 hydroxyl groups.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: Total number of isomers, considering both structural and stereoisomers, of cyclic ethers with the molecular formula C₄H₈O is____
questions.solution: C₄H₈O has one degree of unsaturation, which here is the ring. Five-membered ring: tetrahydrofuran (1). Four-membered ring: 2-methyloxetane, which is chiral (2), and 3-methyloxetane (1). Three-membered ring: 2-ethyloxirane, which is chiral (2); 2,2-dimethyloxirane (1); 2,3-dimethyloxirane as the cis meso form plus the trans pair of enantiomers (3). Total: 1 + 3 + 6 = 10.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
List-I includes starting materials and reagents of selected chemical reactions. List-II gives structures of compounds that may be formed as intermediate products and/or final products from the reactions of List-I.
List-I: (I) 2-(2-(1,3-dioxolan-2-yl)phenyl)acetonitrile —i) DIBAL-H ii) dil. HCl iii) NaBH₄ iv) conc. H₂SO₄→; (II) 2-allylbenzoic acid —i) O₃ ii) Zn, H₂O iii) NaBH₄ iv) conc. H₂SO₄→; (III) methyl 2-(chloromethyl)benzoate —i) KCN ii) H₃O⁺, Δ iii) LiAlH₄ iv) conc. H₂SO₄→; (IV) methyl 2-(2-methoxy-2-oxoethyl)benzoate —i) LiAlH₄ ii) conc. H₂SO₄→
List-II: (P) 2-(2-oxoethyl)benzoic acid; (Q) 2-(2-(hydroxymethyl)phenyl)ethanol; (R) isochromane; (S) 2-(2-hydroxyethyl)benzoic acid; (T) 2-(carboxymethyl)benzoic acid; (U) isochroman-1-one
Which of the following options has correct combination considering List-I and List-II?
questions.solution: (I) DIBAL-H takes the nitrile to an imine, and dilute acid hydrolyses both the imine and the acetal, giving a dialdehyde; NaBH₄ gives diol Q, and acid closes it to the cyclic ether isochromane R. So I → Q, R. (II) Reductive ozonolysis turns the allyl group into CH₂CHO, giving P; NaBH₄ reduces only the aldehyde to give hydroxy acid S, and acid lactonises S to isochromanone U. So II → P, S, U. (III) Cyanide displaces chloride, and hot aqueous acid hydrolyses both the nitrile and the ester to homophthalic acid T; LiAlH₄ gives diol Q, which cyclises to R. So III → T, Q, R. (IV) LiAlH₄ reduces both esters to diol Q, which cyclises to R. So IV → Q, R. Only option C, (II), (P), (S), (U), lists one starting material with compounds it actually forms.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper
